Join fieldwork results to a weighted sample

Source: R/state.R
add_fieldwork.Rd

Fieldwork results usually come back as a table of their own, keyed by an id and in another order. add_fieldwork() adds its columns to sample, row by row through the id, and keeps the sample's rows, their order and the attributes that hold its design. merge() reorders the rows and drops those attributes, and a join that matches a row twice would repeat it.

Usage

add_fieldwork(sample, field, by)

Arguments

sample

A data frame returned by draw() with weights = TRUE, or by as_drawn().

field

A data frame of results: the by columns and the columns to add.

by

The names of one or more columns of sample and field that identify a sampled row.

Value

sample with the other columns of field added after its own.

Details

A sampled row with no row in field gets missing values, as a nonrespondent should: ht_total() refuses them, and ht_mean(na_rm = TRUE) estimates the mean over the rows with a result (see "Missing values and nonresponse" in ht_total()). An id that appears twice in field, an id that is not in sample, a missing id, and a column of field that sample already has are refused. Ids are compared as in as_drawn().

A list from a design with reserve takes fieldwork columns too, such as which units were found unavailable, before use_reserves() turns it into the sample to estimate from.

See also

as_drawn(), ht_mean(), use_reserves()

Examples

pop <- data.frame(id = 1:200, site = rep(c("a", "b"), times = c(150, 50)))
s <- draw(pop, design_stratified("site", n = 40), seed = 1, weights = TRUE)

# Results for 36 of the 40 rows, in the order they came in
field <- data.frame(id = rev(s$id)[1:36], spend = seq(20, 370, by = 10))
s <- add_fieldwork(s, field, by = "id")
ht_mean(s, "spend", na_rm = TRUE)
#> Hajek mean  (stratified design, n = 36)
#>   missing  4 sampled rows left out, assumed missing completely at random
#>   estimate 195
#>   se       10.22661  (analytic)
#>   95% CI  174.2973 to 215.7027  (t, 38 df)
